text: Did you know,

your heart health, kidney health
and diabetes
are all linked?
When one is unhealthy,

it makes the rest of your
body work harder.

Diabetes increases the risk of
heart attack and stroke,

with people twice as likely to
develop heart disease.
High blood sugar from diabetes
can damage blood vessels

and place extra strain
on your heart muscle.
People living with chronic kidney disease

are over 50% more likely
to develop a heart condition.

Damaged kidneys can lead to fluid
and waste buildup in the body,
forcing the heart to work harder.
CKM -
Cardiovascular Kidney Metabolic Syndrome

helps us better understand how
these conditions are connected
so we can manage them together.
Some medicines can treat your diabetes

while also protecting your
heart and kidneys.

The good news is that heart-healthy habits
protect your whole body.

You can reduce your risk
by eating heart-healthy foods,
moving your body daily,
maintaining a healthy weight,
limiting alcohol,
quitting smoking and vaping,
managing stress

and keeping your blood pressure,
cholesterol and blood sugar in check.

Speak to your GP about a
Heart Health Check

to understand your risk of a heart attack
or stroke in the next five years.
During this check, your GP can also

keep track of your kidney health
and diabetes.

Heart-healthy habits
help your whole body thrive.
